nucleus.thesis: Open-source AI should distribute freely with cryptographically enforced accountability chains—decoupling access from gatekeeping while maintaining visible liability.

claims.text: Unrestricted distribution and institutional accountability are treated as mutually exclusive, but can be decoupled through immutable provenance tracking built into model code itself.
Safety coordination needn't require centralized control; transparent lineage, tiered liability frameworks, and cryptographic attribution provide accountability without gatekeeping.
The real design choice is distribution mechanism, not distribution itself. Current policy conflates copying bits with responsibility assignment—a false stacking.
Distributed responsibility architecture (liability traveling with code, not restricted by institutional gatekeepers) addresses both democratization and genuine misuse risk.
Open-source harm insurance pools and decentralized oversight boards make accountability profitable and negligence expensive, replacing scarcity-based control with transparency-based incentives.

shell.topic: Should open-source AI models be freely distributed?

adjacency.target: liability frameworks from centralized to distributed
